title: Counting the Coverage Months Charged Before Cover Began
content:
The coverage months charged before cover began on one of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders are counted against the day the rider took effect and the day the member's Medicare Advantage Health Plans enrollment took effect.

## The rule

**Where the rider took effect after the medical plan enrollment it hangs on took effect**, the coverage months charged before cover began are the whole calendar months from the day that enrollment took effect to the day the rider took effect.

**Where the rider took effect no later than the medical plan enrollment it hangs on did and that enrollment does not stand in force**, no coverage month counts as charged before cover began.

**Otherwise**, the coverage months charged before cover began are the whole calendar months from the day the rider took effect to the day benefits became payable.

## Condition and count

| The day the rider took effect against the day the enrollment took effect | The enrollment's standing | The count |
|---|---|---|
| Later | Any | The whole calendar months from the day the enrollment took effect to the day the rider took effect |
| No later | Not in force | None |
| No later | In force | The whole calendar months from the day the rider took effect to the day benefits became payable |

In every case the count is never fewer than none.

## Worked on hypothetical inputs

- A Medicare Advantage Health Plans enrollment that took effect at the start of January and a rider that took effect at the start of the following July: the rider took effect later, so the count is the whole calendar months between the two days, that is 6.
- A rider that took effect on the same day as an enrollment that no longer stands in force: no coverage month counts as charged before cover began.
- A rider that took effect on the same day as an enrollment still standing in force, benefits having become payable 3 whole calendar months after the rider took effect: the count is 3.
